objective: Try different methods to improve bar accuracy across the available dataset, identify characteristics of high-accuracy tunes, and document methods, failures, results, and limitations.
baseline: ../results: preserved 124-performance pilot, with preferred takes from 75 songs as the primary comparison

scope.primary: All 75 preferred performances; separate async and sync summaries, equal weighting of songs within protocol
scope.secondary: 49 alternate async performances and controlled initial-tempo perturbations for frozen promising candidates
scope.input: Local automatic MIDI transcriptions of bass and horns; no piano MIDI; no future notes or performance annotations in inference
scope.reference: Known unfolded harmonic performance plan, known start, approximate catalog tempo

questions: Does decoding bar posterior mass improve the bar decision compared with choosing the most likely position bin?
Can weaker or confidence-dependent harmonic updates preserve accurate timing while still correcting drift?
Do bass-only, instrument-balanced, or root-weighted harmonic observations help?
Does accounting for trailing-window age improve current position estimates?
Does causal MIDI-onset phase and periodicity add timing evidence that improves following?
Does continuous-position Viterbi beam tracking outperform the probability grid?
Which song, harmony, timing, role, and transcription properties are associated with success or failure within each recording protocol?
protocol: Each run saves all settings and source hashes before executing; successful, failed, and smoke runs are distinguished.
First reproduce the old Maezawa-style primary result exactly before interpreting changes.
Never select a method from the evaluated song's ground-truth labels at inference.
Report exploratory best settings separately from leave-one-song-out selection based on other compositions.
All candidate methods are non-neural and data-independent at inference except their given plan; no pretrained/SOTA claim is made.
Song-property analysis may use reference annotations, but those derived properties never enter the follower.
Because the existing corpus has already been inspected, internal selection is not a pristine external generalization test.
Report exact-bar accuracy, within-two-beat rate, and all-frame position errors together so gains in one metric cannot hide catastrophic errors.
Keep original datasets and baseline outputs unchanged; use independent run directories and save full prediction traces.
required_evidence_for_completion: Completed all-song comparisons for multiple observation and temporal-tracking approaches
Verified causal behavior and baseline reproduction
Transparent selection and secondary robustness results for promising frozen settings
Per-song high/low performance analysis with confounding and data-quality limitations
Reproducible scripts, run logs, configuration/source provenance, per-song tables, and a readable findings report
